content.text: What Each Option Actually Offers: Fonts online

Stripe, PayPal, Gumroad, and Lemon Squeezey each offer a range of features for digital product sellers. Stripe is a payment processor that integrates with numerous e-commerce platforms, while PayPal is a widely accepted payment method with a large user base. Gumroad is a platform specifically designed for creators, offering a simple way to sell digital products. However, these platforms have limitations when it comes to restricted countries. For instance, Stripe only operates in 46 countries, while PayPal can suspend accounts without warning, holding funds for up to 180 days. In contrast, Gumroad has no restrictions on countries, but its fees can be high for larger transactions. Meanwhile, Lemon Squeezey offers a more affordable alternative to Gumroad, but its features are limited compared to other platforms. Ultimately, each platform has its strengths and weaknesses, making it essential for sellers to understand their needs before choosing a platform.
How They Handle Restricted Countries

Restricted countries pose a significant challenge for digital product sellers, as many platforms and payment processors are unavailable or severely restricted. Stripe, for example, operates in only 46 countries, leaving a significant portion of the world's creators without access. PayPal can suspend accounts without warning, holding funds for up to 180 days. In contrast, Gumroad has no restrictions on countries, making it a more attractive option for sellers in restricted regions. However, its fees can be high for larger transactions, which may not be suitable for all sellers. Meanwhile, Lemon Squeezey offers a more affordable alternative to Gumroad, but its features are limited compared to other platforms. By understanding how each platform handles restricted countries, sellers can make informed decisions about their infrastructure architecture.
Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

Payment speed, fees, and real costs are critical considerations for digital product sellers. Stripe and PayPal offer fast payment processing, but their fees can be high, especially for larger transactions. Gumroad's fees are more transparent, but its payment processing times can be slower. Meanwhile, Lemon Squeezey offers more affordable fees, but its payment processing times can be unpredictable. In contrast, Coremerch's Edge Commerce Stack ($197) offers a more affordable and fast payment processing solution, with 5 products loaded, SPF/DKIM/DMARC configured, and end-to-end tested before handoff. By choosing the right infrastructure architecture, sellers can minimize their fees and ensure timely payment processing.
Stripe's geographic exclusion list is a deliberate infrastructure decision — not a temporary gap waiting to be fixed.
Ownership, Automation, and Delivery

Ownership, automation, and delivery are essential considerations for digital product sellers. With Coremerch's Edge Commerce Stack ($197), sellers can own their infrastructure architecture, automating payment processing and delivery with ease. This enables them to focus on creating and marketing their products, rather than worrying about payment processing and delivery. In contrast, other platforms often require sellers to rely on third-party services, which can be unpredictable and unreliable. By choosing Coremerch's Edge Commerce Stack ($197), sellers can ensure timely payment processing, automate delivery, and maintain full ownership of their infrastructure architecture.
Which Architecture to Choose Based on Your Situation

The right infrastructure architecture for digital product sellers depends on their specific needs and circumstances. By understanding the pros and cons of each platform, sellers can choose the best architecture for their situation. For those in restricted countries, Gumroad or Lemon Squeezey may be more suitable options. For those who value fast payment processing and low fees, Coremerch's Edge Commerce Stack ($197) may be the best choice. By considering their needs and circumstances, sellers can choose the right infrastructure architecture and avoid the risks associated with restricted countries.
How do I sell digital products if Stripe is not available in my country?

The direct answer is NOWPayments combined with a sovereign commerce stack. NOWPayments is a crypto payment processor that requires no KYC from merchants and no account creation from buyers. It supports over 300 coins, charges 0.5% per transaction, and sends a webhook to your backend the moment payment confirms on-chain. Your backend — a Cloudflare Worker in Stack 02, a Google Apps Script Web App in Stack 01 — receives the webhook, verifies the transaction hash on the blockchain, logs the order, generates a receipt, and sends the delivery email automatically. There is no platform that can suspend your access, no compliance team that can flag your account, no payout schedule that delays your revenue, and no company that can change the rules on you tomorrow.
Sovereign infrastructure means no single platform decision can cut off your income — the store runs under your own accounts.

Your Deployment Checklist

Accept that no workaround inside conventional payment infrastructure is durable — platforms actively close gaps as they discover them. Create a NOWPayments account and configure wallet addresses for USDT on Tron and Bitcoin as your starting point — these cover the widest range of buyers in restricted markets. Choose your stack: Stack 01 for a self-deployed free setup using GitHub Pages and Google Apps Script, Stack 02 for the Edge Stack deployed by COREMERCH in 48 hours. Configure the NOWPayments webhook endpoint URL in your IPN settings pointing to your backend. Upload your product files to Google Drive or Cloudflare R2. Complete a real mainnet test transaction and confirm the full pipeline: webhook received, transaction verified on-chain, order logged, delivery email sent, download link working. Share your store URL only after the mainnet test passes cleanly.
